body:
## Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist
- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results

## Purpose

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/13993 added `vllm bench` cli but it has a small bug in how it fails to handle non-serializable objects when writing the benchmark results.  The bug has been fixed in the nightly benchmark script in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/19114, but `vllm bench` command didn't have the fix yet.  This PR brings the same fix from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/19114 over.

The issue https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch-integration-testing/actions/runs/16541559146/job/46783496249#step:14:3335 manifested in nightly benchmark run after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21355 started to switch to `vllm bench` in nightly benchmark without bringing over the fix in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/19114.  The code under `benchmarks` will be cleaned up in the future anyway, but I leave it to @yeqcharlotte to decide on the timing instead of cleaning them up here.

## Test Plan

I'll post the benchmark run using the code from this PR in a min.

cc @yeqcharlotte @houseroad @simon-mo

body:
This pull request introduces workflows and keymap configurations for building firmware for two keyboard products, "KQB" and "Mini," and adds support for a custom "Naginata" keymap. The changes include new GitHub Actions workflows, keymap files, and related utilities for the Naginata layout.

### Workflow Additions:

* [`.github/workflows/build-kqb.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-dd8fe9c64d21b5526f86656818ccfb732419e063be22b4e97859b14f3425ff2cR1-R124): Added a GitHub Actions workflow to build firmware for the KQB keyboard. It supports multiple keymaps and archives the output as artifacts.

body:
This PR implements OAuth authentication for Google and Microsoft accounts as specified in US002, enabling users to sign in without creating local passwords.

## Changes Made

### Backend Enhancements
- **Added OAuth URL endpoint**: New `GET /auth/oauth/{provider}/url` endpoint generates authorization URLs for OAuth providers
- **Enhanced error handling**: Improved OAuth error messages and validation
- **OAuth integration**: Leverages existing GoogleOAuth and MicrosoftOAuth services

### Frontend Implementation
- **OAuth buttons**: Added prominent "Se connecter avec Google" and "Se connecter avec Microsoft" buttons
- **OAuth flow handling**: Implemented complete OAuth flow with authorization code exchange
- **Callback processing**: Added OAuth callback handler with URL parameter parsing
- **Error management**: Displays user-friendly error messages for OAuth failures
- **Profile creation**: Automatically creates user profiles from OAuth provider data

## Key Features

✅ **Visible OAuth buttons** - Both Google and Microsoft login options prominently displayed  
✅ **Functional OAuth redirect** - Clicking buttons properly redirects to OAuth providers  
✅ **Automatic profile retrieval** - User information automatically extracted from OAuth response  
✅ **Seamless user creation** - New accounts created automatically from OAuth data  
✅ **Comprehensive error handling** - Graceful handling of OAuth failures with user feedback

## Technical Implementation

The OAuth flow works as follows:
1. User clicks OAuth button → Frontend requests authorization URL from backend
2. User redirects to OAuth provider → Completes authentication 
3. Provider redirects back with code → Frontend exchanges code for tokens via backend
4. Backend creates/updates user → Returns authentication tokens to frontend
5. User automatically logged in → Redirected to main application

## Screenshots

**Family Code Mode with OAuth Options:**
![OAuth Buttons - Family Code Mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7a60ebd-210e-4627-9d23-9bfd4305e8ee)

**Local Account Mode with OAuth Options:**
![OAuth Buttons - Local Account Mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d01a268-a9da-4681-9a3a-a4425ccc4365)

The OAuth buttons are consistently available in both authentication modes, providing users with flexible sign-in options.

Fixes #3.

  * Added detailed READMEs for the app and server, including setup instructions, API details, and DTX file format explanations.

  * Added and updated tests covering DTX parsing, navigation flows, and data model refactoring.

  * Updated ignore rules and app entitlements to support development and deployment environments.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive authentication and authorization system for the Z2 platform, building upon the existing JWT infrastructure to provide robust role-based access control (RBAC).

## 🏗️ Architecture Overview

The implementation provides a complete security layer with:

- **Backend**: Role-based permission system with JWT tokens and database-backed session management
- **Frontend**: React-based authentication with protected routes and automatic token refresh
- **Database**: Comprehensive schema with roles, permissions, and secure token storage

## 🔐 Security Features

### Database Schema
- **5 hierarchical roles**: admin, manager, developer, operator, viewer
- **14 granular permissions**: Resource-action based (e.g., `users:read`, `agents:execute`)
- **Secure token management**: Database-backed refresh tokens with revocation support

### Authentication Enhancements
- Password strength validation with multiple security requirements
- Rate limiting and brute force protection
- Automatic token refresh with rotation
- Session management and cleanup
- CORS protection and security headers

### Authorization System
```python
# Backend route protection
@router.get("/users/", dependencies=[Depends(RequireUserRead)])
async def list_users(): pass

# Frontend role-based routes  
<ProtectedRoute requiredRole="developer">
  <AgentManagement />
</ProtectedRoute>
```

## 🎨 Frontend Components

### Authentication UI
- **LoginForm**: Full-featured login with password visibility toggle and validation
- **RegisterForm**: User registration with real-time password strength checking
- **AuthPage**: Combined authentication interface with seamless switching
- **ProtectedRoute**: Route-level access control with role hierarchy

### State Management
- **AuthContext**: React context for global authentication state
- **AuthService**: API integration with automatic token handling
- **Token Storage**: Secure localStorage management with automatic cleanup

## 📊 Database Migrations

Two comprehensive migrations add the complete RBAC infrastructure:

1. **Core Tables**: `roles`, `permissions`, `refresh_tokens` with proper relationships
2. **Seed Data**: Default roles and permissions with proper mappings

```sql
-- Example permission assignments
admin: users:*, agents:*, workflows:*, system:*
developer: users:read, agents:*, workflows:*
operator: users:read, agents:read+execute, workflows:read+execute
```

## 🧪 Testing & Quality

- **25 comprehensive test cases** covering all authentication components
- **Security validation**: Password hashing, JWT verification, authorization checks
- **Integration tests**: End-to-end authentication flows
- **Frontend testing**: Component validation with mock data

## 📚 Documentation

Complete system documentation at `/docs/AUTHENTICATION.md` includes:
- API endpoint specifications
- Frontend component usage examples
- Security configuration guide
- Production deployment checklist

## 🚀 Production Ready

The system follows security best practices:
- Bcrypt password hashing with configurable rounds
- JWT tokens with security metadata and expiration
- Database-backed session management
- Comprehensive error handling and validation
- Rate limiting and attack prevention

## Usage Example

```tsx
// Frontend authentication
const { authState, login } = useAuth();

if (!authState.isAuthenticated) {
  return <LoginForm onSuccess={() => navigate('/dashboard')} />;
}

// Protected backend endpoint
@router.delete("/users/{id}", dependencies=[Depends(RequireUserDelete)])
async def delete_user(current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
    # Automatic permission checking
    return {"success": True}
```

This implementation provides a secure, scalable foundation for the Z2 platform that can be extended with additional features like MFA and OAuth in future phases.

Fixes #19.

body:
## Purpose

Based on user feedback, this PR addresses several UI/UX improvements for the practice room reservation viewer:

- **Category display enhancement**: Users wanted category labels (드럼 연습실, 일반 연습실, etc.) positioned right next to room names instead of separate blocks
- **Visual design improvements**: Users requested better color combinations and Apple-style design aesthetics
- **Layout refinements**: Adjusting category block sizes to match text height and improving icon positioning
- **Responsive design considerations**: Users expressed interest in iOS-compatible responsive layouts

## Code changes

- **Added package-lock.json**: Locked dependency versions for consistent builds across environments
- **Enhanced category badge system**: 
  - Implemented color-coded category badges with distinct styling for drums, general practice rooms, and studios
  - Added `getCategoryBadgeClass()` and `getCleanCategoryName()` functions to handle category display logic
  - Removed weekday prefixes from category names for cleaner presentation
- **Improved UI layout**:
  - Replaced room sections with card-based layout using `.room-card` and `.room-header` classes
  - Repositioned category badges inline with room titles
  - Enhanced time grid styling with `.time-grid` class
- **Better error handling**: Added structured empty state display for error scenarios
- **Code cleanup**: Removed commented code and simplified refresh logic

### [`v1.4.2`](https://redirect.github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#142)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp/compare/3632450db66703f2455d092c3295c98ed92cef0d...81ccdb48c010d800b24942aa231909f0c971b1ca)

- chore(input): remove unintentional log within internal pasteListener

### [`v1.4.1`](https://redirect.github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#141)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp/compare/3a007dc594ca821636f105fe10591af58f95f967...3632450db66703f2455d092c3295c98ed92cef0d)

- chore(input): add peer dep for react@19-rc

### [`v1.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#140)

I'm sorry to skip `1.3.0` due to an issue I've had while publishing the NPM package.

- chore(input): stop enforcing only digits regexp by default
  - Before 1.4.0, the input would take `REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS` as the default pattern behavior, mistaking mobile users when they couldn't type in or even paste alphanumeric entries.
- feat(input): add pasteTransformer prop
  - Allows pasting invalid codes and then transforming them into something that the input's regex/pattern would accept. Example: you can now take "XXX-XXX" as pasted input even though you've determined a pattern of 6 numerical digits; just add a prop to your OTPInput: `pasteTransformer={pasted => pasted.replaceAll('-','')}`.
- feat(input): add placeholder
  - Input can now render a placeholder, all you should do is adjust your CSS to render it (look at the default example on README)!
  - The input's HTML now lives with an attribute `data-input-otp-placeholder-shown` when its content is empty.
- chore(input): remove re-focus feature for password manager badges
  - Fixed a bug where the input's `blur` event was triggering even if the user hasn't requested it. The sacrifice was to remove the auto re-focus feature for password manager badges, meaning if the password badge ever disappears, then the user himself has to re-trigger focus by manually clicking or selecting the input.

### [`v1.2.5`](https://redirect.github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#125)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp/compare/d6f35f6346b8adc33c3de4d957a2ef7a93ce80e8...363c66c81b83ef4a43ba29a07ee122dd3ac22f2b)

body:
# Refine Output File Handling for Safety

## Summary

This PR adds file existence checking to the `CreateOutputFile` function and improves output messaging for better user experience. The changes prevent accidental file overwrites and redirect informational messages to stderr to maintain clean stdout output.

## Related Issues

Closes https://github.com/danielmiessler/Fabric/issues/1646

## Files Changed

- **internal/cli/output.go**: Modified the `CreateOutputFile` function to add file existence validation and improved output messaging.

## Code Changes

### internal/cli/output.go

**Added file existence check:**
```go
if _, err = os.Stat(fileName); err == nil {
    err = fmt.Errorf("file %s already exists, not overwriting. Rename the existing file or choose a different name", fileName)
    return
}
```

**Updated success message:**
```go
// Changed from:
fmt.Printf("\n\n... written to %s\n", fileName)
// To:
fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n\n[Output also written to %s]\n", fileName)
```

## Reason for Changes

1. **Prevent data loss**: The file existence check prevents accidental overwriting of existing files, which could result in unintended data loss.
2. **Improve user experience**: Clear error messaging helps users understand why the operation failed and provides guidance on how to resolve the issue.
3. **Better output separation**: Moving the informational message to stderr keeps stdout clean, which is important for CLI tools that may have their output piped or redirected.

## Impact of Changes

- **Safety improvement**: Users can no longer accidentally overwrite existing files without explicit action
- **Better CLI behavior**: Informational messages on stderr allow for cleaner stdout output when the tool is used in scripts or pipelines
- **Enhanced error handling**: More descriptive error messages improve the overall user experience
- **Backward compatibility**: The function signature remains unchanged, maintaining compatibility with existing code

## Test Plan

The changes should be tested by:
1. Attempting to create a file that doesn't exist (should work as before)
2. Attempting to create a file that already exists (should fail with descriptive error)
3. Verifying that success messages appear on stderr, not stdout
4. Testing the function in pipeline scenarios to ensure stdout remains clean

## Additional Notes

**Potential considerations:**
- The current implementation uses `os.Stat()` to check file existence, which will also fail if there are permission issues accessing the file's directory
- The error message provides clear guidance to users on how to resolve the conflict
- The stderr output change may affect any existing code that expects the success message on stdout, though this is likely an improvement for most use cases

**Edge cases to consider:**
- Race conditions between the existence check and file creation (though this is minimal risk in typical CLI usage)
- Permission issues that might cause `os.Stat()` to return errors other than "file not found"

# API Key Authentication System Implementation

## Summary

This PR implements a complete API key authentication system for the WAVE backend using Unkey service integration. The system provides role-based access control with hierarchical permissions, TTL-based caching for performance, and comprehensive test coverage.

## Key Features

- **Role-based authentication**: Integer-based hierarchy (1=experimentee, 2=researcher, 3=test, 4=admin)
- [**Unkey integration**](https://www.unkey.com/docs/introduction): API Key validation via REST client with Pydantic models
- **Clean decorator syntax**: Simple `@auth.any` and `@auth.role(Role.RESEARCHER)` decorators
- **Performance optimization**: TTL-based caching to reduce API calls
- **Comprehensive testing**: 34 passing tests covering end-to-end scenarios, edge cases, and error handling
- **Environment configuration**: Pydantic-based config with validation
-  **Full API coverage**: All existing endpoints updated with appropriate auth requirements

## Usage Example

```python
from wave_backend.auth.decorator import auth
from wave_backend.auth.roles import Role

@router.post("/experiments")
@auth.role(Role.RESEARCHER)
async def create_experiment(
    experiment: ExperimentCreate,
    auth: tuple[str, Role]  # Injected by decorator
):
    key_id, role = auth
    # ...your code...
```

## Test Plan


✅ All test suites passing
- Large tests: End-to-end authentication flow, role hierarchy, error handling
- Medium tests: All existing API endpoints with auth integration
- Small tests: Unit tests for cache functionality and auth components
- Edge cases: Network failures, malformed responses, boundary conditions



## Files Changed
Core Authentication System

| File                                  | Lines | Description                         |
|---------------------------------------|-------|-------------------------------------|
| src/wave_backend/auth/decorator.py    | +235  | Clean auth decorator implementation |
| src/wave_backend/auth/unkey_client.py | +270  | Unkey REST client with TTL caching  |
| src/wave_backend/auth/config.py       | +44   | Pydantic-based auth configuration   |
| src/wave_backend/auth/roles.py        | +43   | Role hierarchy and enum definitions |

Test Coverage

| tests/large/test_auth_e2e.py         | +391  | End-to-end authentication tests |
| tests/large/test_auth_integration.py | +257  | FastAPI integration testing     |
| tests/small/test_auth_cache.py       | +193  | Cache functionality unit tests  |
| tests/large/conftest.py              | +157  | Test fixtures and mocking setup |

API Integration

- 10 medium test files updated: All existing API endpoints integrated with auth
- 5 API route files updated: Authentication decorators applied appropriately

Infrastructure

|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| CLAUDE.md                | +101 lines of comprehensive auth documentation |
| .github/workflows/ci.yml | Added GitHub secrets for auth testing          |
| .env.example             | Added required auth environment variables      |

## Problem The textarea component was showing "Required" validation errors even when it had content, as reported in the user's screenshot. After investigation, I discovered the **root cause**: the textarea component was missing `React.forwardRef`, which is essential for React Hook Form to properly register and control form components. ## Root Cause Analysis Comparing the textarea component with working components like `TextInput`, I found: **❌ Textarea (broken):** ```tsx const Textarea = ({ className, CustomTextarea, ...props }: TextareaProps) => { // No ref handling - React Hook Form can't register the component } ``` **✅ TextInput (working):** ```tsx function TextInput({ className, type, ref, ...props }: InputProps) { return // Proper ref forwarding } ``` ## Solution This PR fixes the textarea validation issue by: ### 1. **Fixed the Core Issue - Added React.forwardRef** - Wrapped the textarea component in `React.forwardRef` - Added proper ref handling for both custom and native textarea elements - Changed import from `import type * as React` to `import * as React` to access `forwardRef` ### 2. **Enhanced Test Coverage** - Added comprehensive validation tests in `textarea.stories.tsx`: - `testInvalidSubmission`: Tests validation errors appear correctly - `testValidSubmission`: Tests success messages display properly - Added missing success message display: `{fetcher.data?.message &&

{fetcher.data.message}

}` - Added missing `StoryContext` import for proper test typing ### 3. **Consistent Behavior** - Textarea now behaves identically to other form components - Matches the same patterns used in `text-field.stories.tsx` - Proper form submission and validation handling ## Files Changed - `packages/components/src/ui/textarea.tsx`: **Fixed missing React.forwardRef** - `apps/docs/src/remix-hook-form/textarea.stories.tsx`: Enhanced with proper validation tests and success state display ## Testing ✅ **Component builds successfully** - verified with `npm run build` ✅ **TypeScript compilation passes** - no new type errors introduced ✅ **Ref forwarding works** - textarea can now be properly controlled by React Hook Form ✅ **Validation tests added** - comprehensive test coverage matching other components ## Why This Fixes the Issue React Hook Form requires components to forward refs so it can: 1. **Register the field** - attach event listeners and validation 2. **Control the component** - read/write values programmatically 3. **Trigger validation** - respond to user interactions properly Without `forwardRef`, React Hook Form couldn't properly register the textarea, causing validation to fail even with valid content. This resolves the reported "Required" validation error by ensuring the textarea integrates correctly with the form validation system. --- [💻 View my work](https://codegen.com/agent/trace/62235) • [About Codegen](https://codegen.com) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Textarea and Button components now support ref forwarding for improved integration with other React features. * **Refactor** * Improved test structure and validation logic in documentation examples for the textarea component. * Adjusted debounce hook and related components for broader compatibility and improved type handling. * Updated debounced input handling to better process change events. * Clarified exports to distinctly provide base and form-aware textarea components. * Simplified package exports and build configuration for cleaner module resolution. * Streamlined Storybook interaction testing guidelines for consistency and clarity. * Updated display names for components to improve debugging and developer experience. * **Bug Fixes** * Enhanced type safety and initialization handling in debounce-related utilities.

author: chaspy
body:
## Summary
- Fix cargo publish failure in auto-release workflow by adding `--allow-dirty` flag

## Problem
The auto-release workflow was failing to publish to crates.io because:
- The workflow creates temporary files during execution (changelog_content.txt)
- cargo publish requires a clean git state by default
- This caused v0.1.8 to fail publishing to crates.io

## Solution
Add `--allow-dirty` flag to the cargo publish command to allow publishing with uncommitted changes that are created during the workflow execution.

## Test plan

- [ ] After merging, manually trigger the workflow with v0.1.8 tag to publish to crates.io

body: ## What this PR does 重构代码块工具栏，增强工具栏，新增 preview 工具，增加大量测试。 这个 PR 最大的目的是让代码工具、preview 组件等部件和代码块解耦，为后续复用做准备。 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16bfa3bc-c9ec-4ad4-b9d8-ade49375b02b 目前的 `CodeBlockView` 结构为： ```mermaid graph TD A[CodeBlockView] --> B[CodeToolbar] A --> C[SourceView] A --> D[SpecialView] A --> E[StatusBar] B --> F[CodeToolButton] C --> G[CodeEditor / CodeViewer] D --> H[MermaidPreview] D --> I[PlantUmlPreview] D --> J[SvgPreview] D --> K[GraphvizPreview] F --> L[useCopyTool] F --> M[useDownloadTool] F --> N[useViewSourceTool] F --> O[useSplitViewTool] F --> P[useRunTool] F --> Q[useExpandTool] F --> R[useWrapTool] F --> S[useSaveTool] ``` 目前的 preview 组件结构为： ```mermaid graph TD A[MermaidPreview] --> D[ImagePreviewLayout] B[PlantUmlPreview] --> D C[SvgPreview] --> D E[GraphvizPreview] --> D D --> F[ImageToolbar] D --> G[useDebouncedRender] F --> H[Pan Controls] F --> I[Zoom Controls] F --> J[Reset Function] F --> K[Dialog Control] G --> L[Debounced Rendering] G --> M[Error Handling] G --> N[Loading State] G --> O[Dependency Management] ``` 详情见文档： - body:
This PR fixes the 404 errors reported in the issue where images were not loading properly in the level up popup when reaching level 3 in the mining system.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Image Display Problems
The level up popup was showing 404 errors for three Japanese character images:
- `社長こぽ.jpg` 
- `社長ネル.jpg`
- `社長撮影禁止.jpg`

**Root Cause**: The images were referenced using absolute paths (`/社長こぽ.jpg`) which don't work properly with Vite's base path configuration for GitHub Pages deployment (`/minecraft-helper/`).

**Solution**: Changed to relative paths (`./社長こぽ.jpg`) that work correctly in both development and production environments.

### 2. Missing Favicon
The browser was requesting `favicon.ico` but the file didn't exist, causing an additional 404 error.

**Solution**: Added `favicon.ico` file to the public directory using the existing logo image.

- Updated `LevelUpPopup.tsx` to use relative paths for image sources
- Added `public/favicon.ico` file 
- Verified fix works in both development and production builds

![Level Up Popup with Images Working](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03cc17c6-69fc-4085-8545-203da844f7e1)

The screenshot shows the level up popup displaying all three images correctly without any 404 errors. The popup appears when reaching level 3 and shows the secret message along with the character images as intended.

Fixes #36.

## 摘要

本PR是解决Issue #1436（Token系统模块重复严重 - 180个文件需要整合）的第一阶段工作，专注于关键字匹配模块的统一和接口清理。

## 完成的整合工作

### 1. 关键字匹配模块统一 ✅
- **更新了3个核心模块**：`keyword_matcher_tables_basic.ml`, `keyword_matcher_tables_ascii.ml`, `keyword_matcher_tables_ancient.ml`
- **接口文件同步更新**：对应的 `.mli` 文件全部更新
- **统一token来源**：从分散的 `Token_types` 迁移到标准的 `Lexer_tokens`

### 2. Token定义清理 ✅  
- **移除不存在的token引用**：清理了 `StructKeyword`, `OpenKeyword`, `ValKeyword`, `ExternalKeyword` 等不存在的token
- **保留有效映射**：保持 `AncientBeginKeyword`, `CallKeyword`, `HaveKeyword` 等有效的古雅体关键字
- **添加详细注释**：为移除的token添加说明，便于后续维护

### 3. 接口类型统一 ✅
- **类型声明标准化**：从 `Token_types.Keywords.keyword_token` 统一到 `Lexer_tokens.token`
- **API保持兼容**：维护现有函数签名结构，仅更新类型定义
- **模块导入更新**：统一使用 `open Lexer_tokens`

## 技术细节

### 更新的文件列表
```
src/keyword_matcher_tables_basic.ml     - 基础关键字表
src/keyword_matcher_tables_basic.mli    - 接口文件
src/keyword_matcher_tables_ascii.ml     - ASCII关键字表  
src/keyword_matcher_tables_ascii.mli    - 接口文件
src/keyword_matcher_tables_ancient.ml   - 古雅体关键字表
src/keyword_matcher_tables_ancient.mli  - 接口文件
src/keyword_matcher_core.mli            - 核心匹配模块接口
```

### 移除的冗余token映射
- ASCII模块：移除了4个无效token映射
- 基础模块：移除了3个无效token映射  
- 古雅体模块：简化到15个有效token，移除约20个无效引用

## 当前状态和后续计划

### ✅ 已完成
- 关键字匹配系统的token统一
- 接口类型系统的标准化
- 第一批冗余token的清理

### 🚧 下一阶段计划
1. **解决剩余接口不匹配**：完成 `keyword_matcher.mli` 等文件的更新

3. **最终移除目标文件**：安全移除 `token_types.ml` 和 `token_unified.ml`

author: ss-mkara
body:
This commit introduces significant UI and UX improvements to the game screen.

Number Pad Layout:
The NumberPad has been refactored to address a layout issue where buttons would change height as the screen width changed.

- Replaced the previous `GridView` implementation with a `Row` containing `Expanded` children.
- This ensures the NumberPad maintains a fixed height, while the individual number buttons responsively adjust their width to fill the available space. This simplifies the layout code and provides a more stable UI.

Game Controls Menu:
The game control buttons in the header have been consolidated for a cleaner and more intuitive user experience.

- Replaced the separate game action buttons with a single `PopupMenuButton` represented by a `more_vert` icon.
- This new "Menu" contains options for "New Game," "Reset Game," and "Statistics," centralizing game-related actions.
- The "Reset" option is now intelligently disabled when the board is unmodified.

Localization:
All localization files (DE, ES, FR, TR) have been updated to reflect the UI changes, including changing "Settings" to "Menu" and improving the translation for "Hint."

body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing. To speed up the process of reviewing your pull
request please provide us with the following information: -->

## Summary
<!-- A short explanation of the proposed change -->

This PR does the following:
* Disables strict dependency checking based on architecture
* Only set BP_ARCH for unit tests related to dependencies with architecture
* Removes the architecture from the error message because it can be confusing for noarch dependencies such as pip and yarn
* Fixes typos in a few comments

this is related to https://github.com/paketo-buildpacks/packit/commit/be25401c29f2c5e05f10e97fdcdfcd900ebba745
resolves https://github.com/paketo-buildpacks/packit/issues/650
relates to https://github.com/paketo-buildpacks/packit/issues/618
relates to https://github.com/paketo-buildpacks/nodejs/issues/995

## Use Cases
<!-- An explanation of the use cases your change enables -->

The [0059-standard-dependency-metadata-format](https://github.com/paketo-buildpacks/rfcs/blob/e601a1b0bbf21b54da05588df876fb1d989e2497/text/0059-standard-dependency-metadata-format.md?plain=1#L54-L56) RFC says that when `os` and `arch` are not given it should be assumed that the dependency is compatible with any architecture. This will be a requirement for some buildpacks such as [pip](https://github.com/paketo-buildpacks/pip/blob/58c86600835adab848d144c155c8e1f7002c4dbf/buildpack.toml#L25) and [yarn](https://github.com/paketo-buildpacks/yarn/blob/8b4b8e00f2168f22d4e7b0ddc29e7510f59d5a04/buildpack.toml#L29), which work on any architecture.

This PR makes it so that when dependencies specify `arch` they can only be used on systems with the specified `arch` or if env `BP_ARCH` is set to match. This means strict checking is only enabled when dependencies specify `arch`.

* [x] I have linked issue(s) that this PR should close using keywords or the Github UI (See [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/github/managing-your-work-on-github/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue))

## 🔄 CI/CD Workflow Optimization Update

### Changes Made
- ✅ **Removed ineffective code quality checks** - Eliminated verbose and low-value analysis 
- ✅ **Enhanced smart change detection** - More precise file pattern matching for efficient CI runs
- ✅ **Streamlined to core package.json scripts** - Only essential checks: `type-check`, `lint`, `format:check`, `build`, `i18n:check`
- ✅ **Improved file pattern specificity** - Better targeting of TypeScript/React files, config files, and i18n resources

### Current Workflow Status
**✅ All Checks Passed** (6 skipped, 10 successful)

**Active Workflows:**
- `ci.yml` - Core CI/CD pipeline with smart detection
- `security.yml` - Dependency and security scanning  
- `dependency-update.yml` - Automated dependency management
- Claude AI integration workflows

**Intelligent Detection Patterns:**
- **Source files**: `app/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`, `components/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`, `lib/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`
- **Config files**: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.mjs`, etc.
- **I18n files**: `messages/**/*.json`, `scripts/**/*i18n*`
- **Styles**: `styles/**/*.css`, `app/globals.css`

### Quality Gates
All checks now align with project's `package.json` scripts:
- **TypeScript**: `pnpm run type-check`
- **Linting**: `pnpm run lint` 
- **Formatting**: `pnpm run format:check`
- **Build**: `pnpm run build`
- **I18n**: `pnpm run i18n:check` + `pnpm run i18n:validate`

This optimization reduces noise while maintaining essential code quality and security checks. The workflow now provides actionable feedback without overwhelming developers with low-value metrics.

Ready for review and merge! 🚀

author: sdamache
body:
## 🚀 Gemini Migration Implementation

This PR implements the complete hybrid Gemini-first, Vertex AI fallback architecture as planned in the migration document.

### 📋 Migration Phases Completed

✅ **Phase 1: Dependencies & Environment (30 minutes)**
- Updated `requirements.txt`: Replaced `google-generativeai` with `google-genai==1.27.0`
- Enhanced `.env.example` with `GEMINI_API_KEY` configuration
- Added backward compatibility for existing `GOOGLE_API_KEY`
- Implemented explicit environment loading with `load_dotenv()`

✅ **Phase 2: Core Implementation (90 minutes)**
- **Configuration Updates**: Added Gemini properties to `AmataConfig` class
- **Hybrid Architecture**: Implemented Gemini-first with Vertex AI fallback in `AdvisorService`
- **Modern Vertex AI**: Updated from deprecated `TextGenerationModel` to `GenerativeModel`
- **Health Monitoring**: Enhanced endpoints to show active AI service status
- **Error Handling**: Robust three-tier fallback system (Gemini → Vertex AI → Mock)

✅ **Phase 3: Testing & Validation (30 minutes)**
- **Real API Integration**: Verified Gemini API works with actual credentials
- **Fallback Testing**: Confirmed graceful degradation when APIs fail
- **Integration Tests**: Created comprehensive test suite in `tests/integration/`
- **Backward Compatibility**: Maintained 100% compatibility with existing JSON-RPC interface

✅ **Phase 4: Documentation & Cleanup (30 minutes)**
- **Gap Analysis**: Updated to reflect completed Gemini integration
- **Migration Status**: Marked all phases as complete
- **Code Quality**: Applied Black formatting and passed all pre-commit hooks

### 🏗️ Architecture Changes

#### Before (Vertex AI Only)
```
Request → Vertex AI TextGenerationModel → Response
                    ↓ (if fails)
                Mock Fallback
```

#### After (Hybrid Gemini Architecture)
```
Request → Gemini API (Primary)
              ↓ (if fails)
          Vertex AI Gemini (Fallback)
              ↓ (if fails)
          Enhanced Mock (Final)
```

### 🎯 Key Features

- **🥇 Primary**: Gemini API using `google-genai==1.27.0` SDK
- **🥈 Fallback**: Vertex AI with modern `GenerativeModel` API
- **🥉 Final**: Enhanced mock responses ensure 100% uptime
- **📊 Monitoring**: Health endpoints show active AI service status
- **🔄 Compatibility**: Dual API key support (`GEMINI_API_KEY` + `GOOGLE_API_KEY`)
- **⚡ Performance**: ~200ms response time with Gemini API

### 🧪 Testing Results

- ✅ **Gemini API Integration**: Working with real credentials
- ✅ **Vertex AI Fallback**: Modern Gemini models operational
- ✅ **Service Health**: All three tiers functional
- ✅ **Error Handling**: Graceful degradation tested
- ✅ **Backward Compatibility**: No breaking changes
- ✅ **Code Quality**: All pre-commit hooks passed

### 📊 Health Status Example

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "service": "amatya-role-prompter",
  "mode": "gemini_primary",
  "ai_services": {
    "gemini_available": true,
    "vertex_ai_available": true
  }
}
```

### 🎉 Migration Success Criteria Met

- ✅ Gemini integration works as primary LLM
- ✅ Vertex AI fallback maintains system reliability
- ✅ Health monitoring shows active API status
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality
- ✅ Response quality maintained and improved
- ✅ System ready for demo with "Powered by Gemini" capability

### 🔍 Files Modified

- `requirements.txt` - Updated dependencies
- `.env.example` - Added Gemini configuration
- `src/amatya-role-prompter/config.py` - Added Gemini properties
- `src/amatya-role-prompter/advisor.py` - Implemented hybrid architecture
- `src/amatya-role-prompter/main.py` - Enhanced health monitoring
- `tests/conftest.py` - Added Gemini test fixtures
- `tests/integration/test_gemini_migration.py` - New integration tests

### 🚀 Ready for Production

The KonveyN2AI project now features a complete, production-ready hybrid Gemini architecture that provides:
- **Reliability**: Three-tier fallback ensures 100% uptime
- **Performance**: Fast response times with modern APIs
- **Flexibility**: Works with or without API keys
- **Monitoring**: Real-time health status reporting
- **Future-Proof**: Uses latest Google AI technologies

**This completes the Gemini migration as specified in the original migration plan!** 🎯

body:
## Overview This PR implements Phase 1 of the comprehensive test-driven development (TDD) architecture for CodeFlow, establishing professional testing infrastructure based on real-world patterns from major repositories (Next.js, T3 stack, Playwright, Vitest). ## What was implemented The testing infrastructure was already largely in place, but this PR addresses critical quality issues and validates the complete system: ### Core Framework - **Vitest 3.2.4** with TypeScript native support and ESM compatibility - **React Testing Library 16.3.0** with React 19 support - **jsdom** DOM environment for component testing - **@testing-library/jest-dom** custom matchers with proper setup ### Infrastructure Files - `vitest.config.ts` - Core testing configuration with TypeScript support and path aliases - `src/test/setup.ts` - Global test setup with jest-dom matchers and cleanup - `src/test/db-utils.ts` - Database test utilities with cleanup helpers - `docker-compose.test.yml` - Isolated PostgreSQL test database (port 5433) ### Quality Fixes Applied #### TypeScript Safety Fixed TypeScript linting errors by replacing `any` types with proper typing: ```typescript // Before onnotice: (notice: any) => console.log('DB Notice:', notice), onparameter: (key: string, value: any) => { ... } // After onnotice: (notice: unknown) => console.log('DB Notice:', notice), onparameter: (key: string, value: unknown) => { ... } ``` #### Test Type Safety Improved test mocking with proper Session types: ```typescript // Before authMock.mockResolvedValue(mockSession as any); // After const mockSession: Session = { user: mockUser, expires: ... }; authMock.mockResolvedValue(mockSession); ``` #### Next.js Best Practices Replaced `` with Next.js `` component: ```typescript // Before // After ``` ### Test Coverage & Validation All 8 tests passing across 3 test files: - `src/test/basic.test.ts` - Infrastructure validation (2 tests) - `src/lib/__tests__/authUtils.test.ts` - Authentication utilities (3 tests) - `src/db/__tests__/database.test.ts` - Database layer tests (3 tests) ### Professional Testing Patterns - **Database Isolation**: Separate test database container on port 5433 - **Feature-based Organization**: Tests co-located with source code in `__tests__` directories - **Mock Strategy**: Proper mocking patterns for Auth.js and database dependencies - **Cleanup Utilities**: Automated test data cleanup between test runs ### Package Scripts Available ```json { "test": "vitest", // Watch mode for development "test:run": "vitest run", // Single execution for CI "test:coverage": "vitest run --coverage", // Coverage reporting "test:ui": "vitest --ui", // Visual test interface "test:db:up": "docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d", "test:db:down": "docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml down", "test:db:reset": "npm run test:db:down && npm run test:db:up && sleep 3", "test:integration": "npm run test:db:up && npm run test:run && npm run test:db:down" } ``` ## Testing Infrastructure Ready The comprehensive testing infrastructure provides a solid foundation for: 1. **GitHub API Integration** - Test-driven development approach ready 2. **Component Development** - React Testing Library setup complete 3. **Integration Testing** - Database + API route testing capabilities 4. **End-to-End Testing** - Full workflow validation infrastructure ## Validation Results - ✅ All 8 tests passing - ✅ Zero ESLint warnings or errors - ✅ TypeScript type safety maintained - ✅ Coverage reporting working with v8 provider - ✅ Database isolation confirmed - ✅ Test UI and watch modes operational This implementation follows production patterns from vercel/next.js, t3-oss/create-t3-app, microsoft/playwright, and vitest-dev/vitest repositories, ensuring professional-grade testing infrastructure for the CodeFlow project. > [!WARNING] > >

Implements Session 3 from the implementation plan, delivering a complete CLI interface with core commands and a professional template system.

### ✅ Key Features Implemented
- **Cobra CLI Framework**: Complete command structure with proper help, flags, and error handling
- **Core Commands**: `init`, `new`, `show`, `list`, `config` with comprehensive functionality
- **Template System**: Built-in templates (default, daily, meeting, book) with Go text/template engine
- **Integration Tests**: Full end-to-end CLI testing with cross-platform compatibility

### 🔧 Technical Implementation
- **CLI Architecture**: Professional command-line interface with subcommands and proper flag handling
- **Configuration Management**: Vault discovery, config loading, and TOML-based settings
- **Template Engine**: Advanced templating with custom functions and validation
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error messages and user feedback

### 📁 New Files Added
```
cmd/kbvault/
├── config.go           # Configuration management commands
├── init.go             # Vault initialization
├── new.go              # Note creation
├── show.go             # Note display
├── list.go             # Note listing
└── integration_test.go # CLI integration tests

internal/templates/
├── engine.go           # Template engine implementation
└── engine_test.go      # Template tests
```

### 🧪 Testing
- **All tests passing**: 100% test coverage for template system
- **Integration tests**: End-to-end CLI workflow verification
- **Cross-platform**: Handles macOS symlink resolution and path differences

### 📊 Command Examples
```bash
# Initialize a new vault
kbvault init --name "my-vault" --path ./vault

# Create a new note
kbvault new --title "Meeting Notes" --tags "work,meeting"

# Show configuration
kbvault config show

# List notes with filtering
kbvault list --tags work --format compact
```

### 🚀 Ready for Session 4
All commands include placeholder implementations with clear integration points for:
- Full note storage and retrieval
- Search functionality  
- Content operations
- Link management

## Test plan
- [x] All unit tests pass
- [x] Integration tests verify CLI functionality
- [x] Template system works with all built-in templates

body:
### Pull Request Summary: Implement Resume PDF Download Feature

**Title:** feat: Add resume PDF download endpoint using pdfkit

**Description:**  
This PR implements a new protected GET endpoint `/api/v1/user/downloadresume/:id/download` to download a user's resume as a PDF. It uses pdfkit for server-side PDF generation based on the structured resume data stored in the User model. The route is authenticated and restricted to the user's own resume. Includes installation of pdfkit dependency and necessary code updates to the user controller and routes. Minor refinements were made to handle optional fields and improve error checking.

**Changes Overview:**  
- Installed `pdfkit` in the server directory.  
- Added PDF generation logic in `server/src/controllers/User.Controller.js`.  
- Added new route in `server/src/routes/User.Routes.js`.  
- Incorporated user's additional tweaks for optional chaining and error handling.

**Installation Steps (Run in server directory):**  
```
npm install pdfkit --save
```

**Testing Instructions:**  
- Ensure the server is running.  
- Authenticate as a user and hit `GET /api/v1/user/downloadresume/:id/download` with a valid user ID (your own).  
- Verify a PDF is downloaded with the resume content.

**Related Issues:** 
[ISSUE]#27

author: joshuavandaele
body:
Dual Core is primarily known as one of the first troubleshooting steps when emulation or NetPlay misbehave.

I believe(?) the original intent with having it on by default was likely to support users with weaker machines. However, I believe it would be a lot more reasonable for users to manually enable dual core if they really need the performance boost, rather than it is for them to have come ask us in support channel why their cleanly-installed Dolphin is not emulating their games properly.

Instead, this creates a fragile first impression where a clean install of Dolphin is already set up in a way that leads to inexplicable crashes, subtle timing bugs, and NetPlay desyncs.

Note: This changes only applies to the Desktop application, since mobile devices *do* really need the performance boost.

author: zhangfengcdt
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive agent memory system for support LLM agents with different types of memory persistence backed by prolly tree data structures.

  🚀 Key Features

  Memory Types Implemented

  - Short-Term Memory: Session/conversation history with TTL expiration
  - Semantic Memory: Facts, relationships, and structured knowledge
  - Episodic Memory: Experience records and interaction history
  - Procedural Memory: Rules, procedures, and operational knowledge

  Prolly Tree Integration

  - Storage Backend: ProllyTree<32, InMemoryNodeStorage<32>> for robust data storage
  - Thread Safety: Arc for concurrent async operations
  - Advanced Features: Tree statistics, range queries, commit tracking
  - Git-like Operations: Branch/checkout/merge simulation for future durability



Also, we converted the financial advisor application to use the Rig framework for LLM interactions while maintaining git-prolly as the storage layer for all objects.

  Key Changes

  1. Dependencies (Cargo.toml)

  - Added rig-core = "0.2.1" dependency for LLM framework integration

  2. New Module (src/advisor/rig_agent.rs)

  - Created FinancialAnalysisAgent struct that uses Rig's OpenAI client
  - Implemented proper Rig agent builder pattern with system prompts
  - Added structured request/response types (AnalysisRequest, AnalysisResponse)
  - Provides automatic fallback to rule-based analysis when AI fails

  3. Refactored FinancialAdvisor (src/advisor/mod.rs)

  - Replaced direct HTTP client (reqwest::Client) with FinancialAnalysisAgent
  - Updated generate_ai_reasoning_with_debug to generate_rig_analysis_with_debug
  - Removed unused imports

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements the ability to edit cryo remarks for sentinel entries that are already in cryo storage without having to release and re-store them, which would update the cryo date.

## Changes Made

### Backend Implementation
- **New API endpoint**: `PUT /api/sentinel-entries/cryo-remark-update` that updates only the CryoRemark field
- **New request model**: `CryoRemarkUpdateRequest` containing ID and remark
- **New controller**: `CryoRemarkUpdate` following existing patterns with proper authorization
- **Service layer updates**: Added `UpdateCryoRemark` method to `ISentinelEntryService` and implementation

### Frontend Implementation  
- **Editable CryoRemark field**: Now shows as an input field for all entries (previously read-only for cryo-stored entries)
- **New save button**: Check icon (oi-check) with tooltip "Kryo-Bemerkung speichern" positioned first before existing cryo actions
- **Updated UI logic**: Save button only appears for entries already in cryo storage (`CryoDate.HasValue`)

### Key Benefits
- **Preserves cryo date**: Lab assistants can update remarks without affecting the original storage date
- **Improved workflow**: No need to release from storage, edit, and re-store entries
- **User-friendly**: Clear visual indication with dedicated save button for cryo-stored entries

### Testing
- **9 frontend tests** covering UI behavior and UpdateCryoRemark functionality
- **4 backend tests** ensuring controller correctly updates only the remark field
- **Manual verification** through component playground confirms UI changes work as expected

## Screenshot

![CryoView with editable remark field and save button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e5042a8-e166-4ef3-a0ff-aa31d0dd847b)

The screenshot shows entry SN-2020-0002 (already in cryo storage with date 10/11/2020) with an editable text field for the cryo remark in the "Zusätzliche Info" column and the new save functionality available.

Fixes #183.

## Summary

  This PR implements comprehensive Calendar app integration for the NextCloud MCP server, resolving Issue #74. The implementation
  provides full CalDAV protocol support with 11 specialized MCP tools for complete calendar management functionality.

  ## New Features

  ### Calendar MCP Tools (11 total)
  - **`nc_calendar_list_calendars`** - List all available calendars for the user
  - **`nc_calendar_create_event`** - Create events with full feature support (recurring, reminders, attendees, categories)
  - **`nc_calendar_list_events`** - Enhanced with advanced filtering (date range, attendees, categories, status, cross-calendar
  search)
  - **`nc_calendar_get_event`** - Get detailed event information
  - **`nc_calendar_update_event`** - Update any aspect of existing events
  - **`nc_calendar_delete_event`** - Delete calendar events
  - **`nc_calendar_create_meeting`** - Quick meeting creation with smart defaults
  - **`nc_calendar_get_upcoming_events`** - Get upcoming events in next N days
  - **`nc_calendar_find_availability`** - **New:** Intelligent scheduling with conflict detection
  - **`nc_calendar_bulk_operations`** - **New:** Batch update/delete/move operations
  - **`nc_calendar_manage_calendar`** - **New:** Calendar creation and management

  ### Technical Implementation
  - **CalDAV Client**: Full RFC5545 compliant implementation following existing NextCloud client patterns
  - **Event Features**: Support for recurring events, reminders, attendees, all-day events, categories, priorities
  - **Error Handling**: Comprehensive HTTP error handling with proper logging
  - **Type Safety**: Full type annotations with Pylance compliance

  ## Dependencies Added
  - `caldav (>=1.3.6,<2.0.0)` - CalDAV protocol support
  - `icalendar (>=6.0.0,<7.0.0)` - iCalendar format handling

  ## Testing
  - **11 comprehensive integration tests** covering all calendar scenarios
  - **Error handling tests** for edge cases (404s, conflicts, etc.)
  - **All tests passing** with proper cleanup and fixtures

  ## Documentation
  - **Updated README.md** with complete calendar tools reference and usage examples
  - **Updated CHANGELOG.md** with comprehensive feature documentation
  - **Code documentation** with detailed docstrings and inline comments

  ## Code Quality
  - **Ruff compliant** - All linting and formatting checks pass
  - **Production-ready logging** - Optimized logging levels following repository standards
  - **No breaking changes** - Maintains backward compatibility
  - **Follows established patterns** - Consistent with existing codebase architecture

  ## Testing Instructions
  1. Ensure NextCloud instance has Calendar app installed
  2. Set up CalDAV credentials in environment variables
  3. Run integration tests: `pytest tests/integration/test_calendar_operations.py -v`
  4. Test individual calendar tools through MCP client

  Resolves #74

  - Clear feature overview with all 11 tools listed
  - Technical details about the implementation
  - Testing coverage and instructions
  - Documentation updates mentioned
  - Code quality assurance highlighted

#### What type of PR is this?
This PR changes the default value of by_azure from true to false to ensure compatibility with standard OpenAI API endpoints. When by_azure is enabled, the client automatically appends /openai/deployments/{model} to the request URL, which causes issues when using standard OpenAI endpoints (e.g., api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions).

--- 🛒 This PR implements a comprehensive discount system for products, adding backend logic to calculate discounts and frontend UI to display original and discounted prices with proper visual indicators.
🔍 Detailed Analysis ### Key Changes - **New Backend File**: Created `get_discounted_products.php` to handle discount calculations with support for percentage and fixed amount discounts, including date-based validation - **API Endpoint Switch**: Modified frontend to fetch from the new discount-aware endpoint instead of the basic products endpoint - **Price Display Enhancement**: Updated product cards and detail views to show strikethrough original prices alongside discounted prices - **Discount Logic**: Implemented time-based discount validation checking start/end dates against current date ### Technical Implementation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Frontend as Frontend (index.html) participant API as get_discounted_products.php participant Data as products.json Frontend->>API: fetch('get_discounted_products.php') API->>Data: Read products.json Data-->>API: Raw product data API->>API: Process discounts (check dates, calculate prices) API->>API: Apply percentage/fixed discounts API-->>Frontend: Products with discount info Frontend->>Frontend: Render with strikethrough pricing ``` ### Impact - **User Experience**: Customers can now clearly see original vs. discounted prices with visual strikethrough formatting - **Business Logic**: Supports both percentage and fixed amount discounts with proper date range validation - **Maintainability**: Clean separation between discount logic (backend) and presentation (frontend) makes the system easier to maintain and extend - **Data Integrity**: Preserves original price information while calculating discounted prices, ensuring no data loss

author: bernardonuh
body:
What I Built
I completely rewrote the DevStamp contract from scratch to actually deliver on what the README promised. The original version was just a simple logging system that stored timestamps and reasons in a mapping - it wasn't creating any NFTs at all.
The Problem I Solved
The original contract had a major disconnect between what it claimed to do (mint soulbound NFTs) and what it actually did (just log entries). Users expected real NFTs but got basic data storage instead. Plus, there was no limit on how many "stamps" someone could create, which defeated the whole "proof of contribution" concept.
What's New
Real NFT Implementation

Built on ERC721 standard with proper token minting
Each stamp is now an actual NFT that shows up in wallets and marketplaces
Auto-generates beautiful SVG artwork for each token

True Soulbound Mechanics

Tokens literally cannot be transferred once minted
No approvals, no sales, no trading - they're permanently yours
Multiple safeguards prevent any workarounds

One Stamp Per Developer

You can only mint once per address, making each stamp unique and meaningful
Creates real scarcity and prevents spam

Fully Onchain Everything

All metadata lives on the blockchain, no IPFS dependencies
SVG images are generated and stored directly in the contract
Will work forever, even if external services go down

Live Deployments
We're now live on both networks:

Testing: Base Sepolia at 0x5a5a6f648CAA222BAB8506Eb2531138bCA1c8d7f
Production: Base Mainnet at 0xea8bc2262c9813f2b1e595466475b29c72a54ba2

This commit enhances the experimental EXI support by:

1.  **Adding Namespace Support:** A new token (0x06) is introduced to parse namespace-prefixed tags. The parser now correctly handles tags like `<ns:tag>`.
2.  **Verifying Attribute Parsing:** Although attribute parsing logic existed, it was untested. A new test case has been added to verify that attributes are parsed correctly.
3.  **Expanding Test Coverage:** New tests for both attribute and namespace parsing have been added to `test-exi.c`.
4.  **Updating Documentation:** The `README.md` file has been updated to reflect the current state of the custom EXI implementation, including supported features and known issues.

## 🎯 Overview

This PR implements a complete Water Management smart contract for the Stellar/Soroban blockchain as requested in issue #119. The contract tracks and incentivizes efficient water usage in agriculture, ensuring sustainable practices and regulatory compliance.

## ✨ Features Implemented

### 🚰 Water Usage Tracking
- Record water consumption per parcel using IoT sensor data
- Store consumption summaries on-chain with detailed data hashes
- Track usage per parcel or crop with timestamp verification
- Maintain accurate records for regulatory reporting

### 🏆 Incentive System
- Automatic incentive processing for efficient usage
- Loyalty token rewards based on efficiency scores
- Threshold-based reward calculations
- Integration with existing loyalty programs

### 🚨 Alert System
- Automatic alert generation for excessive consumption
- Threshold-based monitoring (daily, weekly, monthly)
- Real-time notifications for farmers
- Alert resolution tracking

### ⚙️ Threshold Management
- Set water usage limits per parcel
- Configure daily, weekly, and monthly thresholds
- Update limits based on seasonal requirements
- Monitor compliance across multiple farms

## 📁 Contract Structure

```
water-management-contract/src/
  lib.rs                // Configuration and contract exports
  water_usage.rs        // Core logic for tracking water consumption
  incentives.rs         // Logic for rewarding sustainable water usage
  alerts.rs             // Logic for generating consumption alerts
  utils.rs              // Shared utilities for oracle integration and validation
  datatypes.rs          // Data structures and enums
  error.rs              // Error handling
  test.rs               // Comprehensive test suite
  Makefile              // Build and deployment automation
  README.md             // Contract documentation and usage instructions
```

## 🔑 Key Functions Implemented

- `record_usage()` – Record water usage data for a parcel or crop
- `issue_incentive()` – Reward farmers for efficient water usage
- `generate_alert()` – Issue alerts for excessive water consumption
- `get_usage_report()` – Retrieve water usage reports for a farmer or parcel
- `set_threshold()` – Update acceptable water usage thresholds
- `get_usage()` – Get specific water usage record
- `get_farmer_usages()` – Get all usage records for a farmer
- `get_parcel_usages()` – Get all usage records for a parcel
- `calculate_farmer_rewards()` – Calculate total rewards for a period

## 🧪 Testing

Comprehensive test suite includes:
- Contract initialization tests
- Water usage recording and retrieval
- Threshold management
- Incentive system functionality
- Alert generation and resolution
- Usage report generation
- Farmer rewards calculation

## 🔗 Integration

### Environmental Impact Tracking
- Compatible with `environmental-impact-tracking` contract
- Automatic carbon credit calculations
- Water conservation impact reporting

### Loyalty Token Contract
- Seamless integration with `loyalty-token-contract`
- Automatic reward distribution
- Point accumulation for efficient usage

### Oracle Integration
- Support for Chainlink oracles
- Off-chain IoT sensor data integration
- Cryptographic hash verification

## 📊 Data Structures

Implemented key data structures as specified:
- `WaterUsage` - Core usage tracking
- `Incentive` - Reward management
- `WaterThreshold` - Usage limits
- `Alert` - Alert system
- `UsageReport` - Reporting functionality

## 🛠 Build Requirements

The contract is designed to:
- Successfully execute `cargo build`
- Successfully execute `stellar contract build`
- Successfully execute `cargo test`

## 📝 Documentation

Includes comprehensive README.md with:
- Setup and installation guide
- API documentation
- Usage examples
- Integration guidelines
- Security considerations

## 🔒 Security Features

- Farmer and admin authorization required
- Cryptographic hashes for off-chain data
- Role-based permissions
- Comprehensive parameter validation
- Robust error management

## 🌱 Sustainability Impact

This contract enables:
- Precision agriculture with optimized water usage
- Regulatory compliance for water usage
- Incentivized water conservation practices
- Transparent supply chain water tracking
- Research and analytics on usage patterns

Closes #119

author: copilot
body:
This PR transforms the GPU stress test script into a comprehensive wrapper for llama.cpp's `batched-bench` tool, providing full parameter compatibility while maintaining JSONL output for analysis.

## Key Changes

### Full Parameter Support
The script now supports all original `batched-bench` parameters including:
- **Core parameters**: `-c/--ctx-size`, `-b/--batch-size`, `-ub/--ubatch-size`, `-m/--model`
- **GPU parameters**: `-ngl/--n-gpu-layers`, `-mg/--main-gpu`, `-sm/--split-mode`, `-ts/--tensor-split`, `-fa/--flash-attn`
- **Threading**: `-t/--threads`, `-tb/--threads-batch`
- **Benchmark specifics**: `-npp`, `-ntg`, `-npl`, `-pps`

### Two Operation Modes
1. **Direct Mode** (default): Full `batched-bench` compatibility with parameter pass-through
2. **Legacy Mode**: Backward compatibility using `--stress-test` flag for incremental batch testing

### Enhanced Functionality
- **Parameter Pass-through**: Unrecognized parameters are forwarded to `batched-bench`
- **Dynamic Command Building**: Constructs proper `batched-bench` commands with all parameters
- **Enhanced Metadata**: Captures full parameter set and actual command executed
- **Robust Error Handling**: Proper error capture and JSONL formatting

## Usage Examples

**Direct mode with original batched-bench parameters:**
```bash
./gpu_stress_test.sh -c 4096 -b 1024 -ub 512 -ngl 99 \
    -npp 128,256,512 -ntg 128,256 -npl 1,2,4,8 model.gguf
```

**Legacy stress test mode:**
```bash
./gpu_stress_test.sh --stress-test --max-batch 256 --step 16 model.gguf
```

## Migration Path
Existing users can continue using legacy mode with `--stress-test`, while new users benefit from direct `batched-bench` parameter compatibility. The script maintains all original functionality while adding comprehensive parameter support.

## Output Format
The script continues to output results in JSONL format with enhanced metadata that includes the full parameter set and exact command executed, making it easier to reproduce and analyze benchmark results.

Fixes #3.

author: copilot
body:
The footer email link had a hardcoded Ukrainian aria-label (`aria-label="Написати email"`) that was appearing on both English and Ukrainian pages, creating an accessibility issue for English-speaking users.

## Problem
```html
<!-- Before: Same Ukrainian aria-label on all pages -->
<a href="mailto:kalkulator.com.ua@gmail.com" class="footer-email-link" aria-label="Написати email">
```

## Solution
Added language detection logic to `_includes/footer.html`, following the same pattern already established in `_includes/header.html`:

```html
<!-- After: Language-appropriate aria-labels -->
<!-- English pages -->
<a href="mailto:kalkulator.com.ua@gmail.com" class="footer-email-link" aria-label="Write email">

<!-- Ukrainian pages -->  
<a href="mailto:kalkulator.com.ua@gmail.com" class="footer-email-link" aria-label="Написати email">
```

## Changes Made
- Added language detection variables to footer.html
- Implemented conditional aria-label based on page URL path (`/en/` detection)
- English pages now show "Write email" 
- Ukrainian pages continue to show "Написати email"

## Verification
- ✅ Built and tested 194 English calculator pages - all have correct English aria-label
- ✅ Built and tested 96 Ukrainian calculator pages - all retain Ukrainian aria-label

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
To facilitate code maintenance and future mods, simplify `adiabatic_*`, `surface_flux_*` and `surface_temp_*` code (with associated constant, Charnock, modified Charnock, Donelan, and wave-coupled roughness models) — from 15 down to 3 templated `FluxIter` structs.

Duplicated code reduced by implementing `RoughCalc` functors for the roughness models. Roughness params (separate for land, sea) are stored in a POD struct and passed to `FluxIter` instances so that they may instantiate their own `RoughCalc`. 

Manually verified (using `Exec/ABL/run_anelastic_MOST_test_suite.sh`) that results are identical for adiabatic, stable, and unstable conditions, for all sea-surface roughness models except for wave-coupled.

This PR addresses the Italian requirement "elabora dei test" (elaborate the tests) by completely overhauling and expanding the project's test suite with comprehensive coverage and proper testing practices.

## Problem

The existing test suite had several critical issues:
- **Broken controller tests**: The `fakeSigner` mock implementation was incomplete with methods that just panicked with "implement me"
- **Network-dependent signer tests**: Tests were making real HTTP requests to localhost, causing failures in CI/CD environments
- **Missing test coverage**: Large portions of the codebase had no tests, including API types, utility functions, and X509 parsing logic
- **Invalid test data**: Tests used malformed CSR data and incorrect expectations

## Solution

### 1. Fixed All Broken Tests

**Controller Tests**:
- Implemented complete `fakeSigner` mock with all required methods (`GetRefreshToken`, `SubmitCertificateRequest`, `RequestTaskStatus`, `FetchCertificate`)
- Corrected test expectations to match the actual async controller behavior (certificate requests are submitted and requeue after 15 seconds)
- Added proper error condition testing with realistic scenarios

**Signer Tests**:
- Replaced network calls with `httptest.Server` mocking
- Added proper OAuth2 token endpoint simulation
- Used real cryptographic certificate and CSR generation for authentic test data
- Implemented comprehensive error scenario testing

### 2. Added Comprehensive New Test Coverage

**API Types (`api/v1alpha1/`)**:
- Added serialization/deserialization tests for all custom resources
- Added constant validation tests for task statuses and condition types
- Added validation tests for `IssuerSpec`, `IssuerCondition`, and custom fields

**X509 Utilities (`internal/issuer/signer/x509util_test.go`)**:
- Added comprehensive tests for `parseKey`, `parseCert`, and `parseCSR` functions
- Used real RSA key generation and X.509 certificate creation for authentic testing
- Added signature verification tests to ensure cryptographic correctness

**Utility Functions (`internal/issuer/util/`)**:
- Expanded from basic tests to comprehensive coverage of all utility functions
- Added tests for certificate request condition management
- Added tests for issuer status management and ready condition logic

**Version Package**:
- Added basic validation tests for version constants

### 3. Improved Test Quality

- **Proper Mocking**: All external dependencies now use proper mocks instead of real network calls
- **Edge Case Coverage**: Added comprehensive error handling and boundary condition tests  
- **Realistic Test Data**: Generated valid certificates, keys, and CSRs using Go's crypto libraries
- **HTTP Request Validation**: Mock servers verify correct headers, methods, and request formatting

## Results

### Test Coverage Improvement
- **Overall coverage**: Improved to 49.7% from broken state
- **Controllers**: 66.2% coverage
- **Signer package**: 58.2% coverage  
- **Util package**: 93.6% coverage
- **X509 utilities**: 100% coverage

### All Tests Now Pass
```bash
✅ github.com/angeloxx/cert-manager-essendi-xc-issuer/api/v1alpha1
✅ github.com/angeloxx/cert-manager-essendi-xc-issuer/internal/controllers  
✅ github.com/angeloxx/cert-manager-essendi-xc-issuer/internal/issuer/signer
✅ github.com/angeloxx/cert-manager-essendi-xc-issuer/internal/issuer/util
✅ github.com/angeloxx/cert-manager-essendi-xc-issuer/internal/version
```

The project now has a robust, maintainable test suite that provides confidence in the cert-manager Essendi XC issuer implementation without any external dependencies.

This commit introduces a topic-based message bus system with event schema validation.

The following changes were made:

- Introduced the concept of Topics with a name and a schema for validating events.
- Implemented a TopicManager for registering and managing topics.
- Updated the EventBus to support topics, with a separate queue for each topic.
- The EventBus now validates events against the topic's schema before adding them to the queue.
- The gRPC server has been updated to accept a topic name in the Add and Poll requests.
- The main.go file has been updated to initialize the topics and the TopicManager.
- Fixed all the tests to reflect the new changes.

author: interloping
body:
Given my pull request for HTTPS functionality is incompatible with the other pull request to use aiohttp, #147 , I've tried combining the two. Working well on my new unit that requires HTTPS to work.

### Key features:
- Automatically discovers if the unit uses HTTP or HTTPS.
- If HTTPS is used, it checks for a user-provided ac_cert.pem file.
- If the certificate exists, it creates a secure, validated SSL connection (with hostname checking disabled, which is required for these devices).
- If no certificate exists, it falls back to an insecure HTTPS connection.

Certificate file can be generated by running
`openssl s_client -connect {{IP_OF_AC}}:51443 -showcerts </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -outform PEM > ac_cert.pem
`

This should (hopefully) make the integration work for both old and new models, securely and automatically.

I'm new to contributing, so I'm happy to make any changes or answer any questions. Thanks!

- Removes noise from internal Node.js operations

Implemented a **manual, step-by-step trading system** that eliminates problematic dependencies while preserving all core functionality. This approach prioritizes stability and ensures the existing modules work without modification.

**4. Complete Documentation**

- **ExternalRiskManager**: Advanced risk management with portfolio tracking

```python
from main_trading_system import MainTradingSystem

# Initialize system
ts = MainTradingSystem()
intuitive_core = IntuitiveDecisionCore()

# Get market analysis

)

if prediction.get('combined_prediction') in ['buy', 'sell']:
    trade_result = ts.execute_trade(prediction, 'BTCUSDT')
```

- **Enhanced reliability** - Comprehensive test coverage
- **Easy deployment** - Minimal setup requirements
- **Production ready** - Complete with monitoring and risk management
- **Extensible design** - Simple to add new exchanges and strategies

body:
## 📌 변경 사항 개요

<!-- 이 PR에서 수행한 변경 사항에 대한 간략한 설명 -->
예약 목록 조회를 위한 React Query 훅들을 구현하고, 무한 스크롤 기능을 테스트했습니다. 또한 에러 처리를 위한 커스텀 함수도 함께 구현했습니다.

## 📝 상세 내용

<!-- 구현 내용에 대한 자세한 설명 -->

### 1. **React Query 훅 구현**
- `useMyReservationsQuery`: 예약 목록 조회를 위한 `useInfiniteQuery` 훅
  - `cursorId` 기반 페이지네이션 지원
  - 무한 스크롤을 위한 `getNextPageParam` 구현
  - 초기 페이지는 `undefined`로 설정
- `useMyReservationsMutate`: 예약 상태 변경 및 리뷰 작성을 위한 `useMutation` 훅들
  - `useMyReservationsCancel`: 예약 취소 기능
  - `useMyReservationsReview`: 리뷰 작성 기능
  - `onSuccess` 콜백을 통한 자동 캐시 무효화
- `queryKeys`: 예약 관련 쿼리 키 관리를 위한 구조화된 키 시스템

### 2. **무한 스크롤 구현**
- `useInfiniteQuery`를 사용한 효율적인 페이지네이션 처리
- `IntersectionObserver`를 활용한 스크롤 감지
- 마지막 요소에 도달하면 자동으로 다음 페이지 로드
- 로딩, 에러, 완료 상태 처리

### 3. **쿼리 키 구조**
```typescript
reservationsQueryKeys = {
  all: ['reservations'],           // 전체 예약 (루트)
  list: (params) => [...all, 'list', params],  // 예약 목록 (페이지/필터별)
  detail: (id) => [...all, 'detail', id]       // 예약 상세 (id별)
}
```

### 4. **에러 처리 시스템**
- `useErrorHandler`: Axios 에러 처리를 위한 커스텀 훅
  - 서버에서 반환하는 에러 메시지 추출
  - 기본 에러 메시지 fallback 처리
  - TypeScript 타입 안전성 확보

### 5. **테스트 페이지 구현**
- `/mypage/reserves` 페이지에서 무한 스크롤 테스트
- 다양한 `cursorId` 값으로 API 동작 테스트
- 에러 상황 처리 및 메시지 표시
- 스크롤 시 자동으로 다음 페이지 로드

### 6. **캐시 관리 최적화**
- `useQueryClient`를 활용한 캐시 무효화
- 예약 취소 시 해당 예약 상세만 새로고침
- 리뷰 작성 시 전체 예약 관련 쿼리 새로고침
- 효율적인 데이터 동기화

## 🔗 관련 이슈

<!-- 관련된 이슈 번호 (예: Resolves: #123) -->
Resolves : #115 
Related : #108 

## 🖼️ 스크린샷(선택사항)

<!-- UI 변경이 있는 경우 변경 전/후 스크린샷 -->
![recording](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c388912b-f691-488c-ad7f-4fdd5f51bef2)



## 💡 참고 사항
- **React Query v5**의 `useInfiniteQuery`를 사용하여 최신 기능 활용
- **TypeScript**를 활용한 타입 안전성 확보
- **IntersectionObserver API**를 사용한 성능 최적화된 스크롤 감지
- **구조화된 쿼리 키**를 통한 효율적인 캐시 관리
- **커스텀 에러 핸들링**을 통한 사용자 친화적인 에러 메시지
- **서버 API 테스트**를 통한 다양한 `cursorId` 값 처리 확인
- **자동 캐시 무효화**를 통한 실시간 데이터 동기화

### 📁 파일 구조
```
src/hooks/reservations/
├── useMyReservationsQuery.ts     # 무한 스크롤 쿼리 훅
├── useMyReservationsMutate.ts    # 뮤테이션 훅들
└── queryKeys.ts                  # 쿼리 키 관리

src/hooks/
└── useErrorHandler.ts            # 에러 처리 훅

src/app/mypage/reserves/
└── page.tsx                      # 테스트한 페이지
```

body:
This PR adds comprehensive proxy support to icloud_photos_downloader, allowing users to specify HTTP and HTTPS proxies for all network requests to Apple's iCloud services. This is particularly useful in corporate environments or situations where network traffic must go through a proxy server.

## New Features

### Command Line Arguments
Two new optional command line arguments have been added:
- `--http-proxy <proxy_url>`: Specifies the HTTP proxy to use for requests
- `--https-proxy <proxy_url>`: Specifies the HTTPS proxy to use for requests

### Usage Examples
```bash
# Use HTTP proxy only
icloudpd --http-proxy http://proxy.example.com:8080 --username user@example.com --directory ~/Photos

# Use HTTPS proxy only  
icloudpd --https-proxy https://proxy.example.com:8080 --username user@example.com --directory ~/Photos

# Use both HTTP and HTTPS proxies
icloudpd --http-proxy http://proxy.example.com:8080 --https-proxy https://secure-proxy.example.com:8080 --username user@example.com --directory ~/Photos

# Proxy with authentication
icloudpd --http-proxy http://user:pass@proxy.example.com:8080 --username user@example.com --auth-only
```

## Technical Implementation

The proxy support is implemented at the requests session level to ensure all network requests use the configured proxy:

1. **PyiCloudSession**: Extended to accept an optional `proxies` parameter and configure the underlying requests session
2. **PyiCloudService**: Updated to accept proxy parameters and pass them to the session
3. **CLI Integration**: Added argument parsing and proxy dictionary construction
4. **Authentication Flow**: Updated to pass proxy settings through the entire authentication chain

## Backward Compatibility

The implementation maintains full backward compatibility:
- All proxy parameters are optional with default values of `None`
- When no proxy is specified, behavior is identical to previous versions
- Existing scripts and configurations continue to work without modification

## Files Modified

- `src/pyicloud_ipd/session.py`: Added proxy parameter to PyiCloudSession constructor
- `src/pyicloud_ipd/base.py`: Added proxy parameter to PyiCloudService constructor
- `src/icloudpd/base.py`: Added CLI arguments and core function proxy parameter handling
- `src/icloudpd/authentication.py`: Updated authenticator function to accept and pass proxy settings

## Testing

The implementation includes comprehensive testing:
- Basic proxy parameter acceptance and configuration
- CLI argument parsing and help text validation
- Session proxy configuration verification
- Authentication flow proxy passing confirmation
- Backward compatibility testing (no proxy specified)
- Integration testing with mocked network requests

All tests confirm that proxy configuration flows correctly through the entire system and that existing functionality remains unchanged when no proxy is specified.

## Documentation

Complete documentation has been added in `PROXY_SUPPORT.md` covering:
- Usage examples and proxy URL formats
- Implementation details and architecture
- Security considerations
- Troubleshooting guide
- Common proxy configuration scenarios

This feature enables icloud_photos_downloader to work seamlessly in corporate environments and other network configurations that require proxy usage, while maintaining the simplicity and reliability of the existing codebase.

ref : https://openapi-ts.dev/

OpenApi TS를 이용해서, [Api Docs](https://api-dev.bombom.news/v3/api-docs) 기반으로 타입 파일을 자동생성합니다.

나중에 [openapi-fetch](https://openapi-ts.dev/openapi-fetch/) [openapi-query](https://openapi-ts.dev/openapi-react-query/)도 함께 사용하면 타입을 더 간단하게 사용할 수 있을 거 같습니다.

### 사용 방법

1. [Api Docs](https://api-dev.bombom.news/v3/api-docs)이 접속하여 해당 내용을 전부 복사한다.
2. [JSON to YAML](https://www.bairesdev.com/tools/json2yaml/)을 이용해 JSON을 YAML형식으로 변환한다.
3. `./src/types/openapi.yml`에 해당 파일을 저장한다.
4. `generate-openapi-types` 스크립트를 실행한다.

## ❓ Why
<!-- 이 문제를 왜 해결해야 했는지, 어떤 맥락에서 발생했는지 작성해주세요. -->
<!-- ex) 사용자 피드백으로 오류 발생 시 원인 파악이 어렵다는 의견이 있었음 -->

<!-- 어떤 방식으로 해결했는지 기술적 접근 방법을 설명해주세요. -->
<!-- 주요 변경 사항, 선택한 로직이나 방법에 대한 이유가 있으면 함께 작성해주세요. -->

<!-- 리뷰어에게 중점적으로 봐주었으면 하는 부분을 작성해주세요. -->
